## Introduction

`sharepointr` uploads, downloads, lists, and manages files on SharePoint
document libraries from R. Build one `auth` object with `sharepoint_auth()`,
then pass it to every other function.

Three authentication methods are supported — pick based on how you'll run
the script:

| Method | Setup | Needs admin? | Unattended? | Backend |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cookie (`fedauth`/`rtfa`) | Copy two values from your browser | No | No | REST only |
| Client secret | Entra ID app registration + secret | Yes, once | Yes | Graph or REST |
| Certificate | Entra ID app registration + certificate | Yes, once | Yes | Graph or REST |

## Option 1: Cookie authentication

This reuses your own already-signed-in SharePoint browser session — no app
registration, no admin. Best for interactive or one-off scripts; not
suited to unattended jobs, since the cookies expire on your tenant's normal
sign-in-frequency schedule and there's no way to refresh them without
signing in again.

1. Sign in to your SharePoint site in a browser as you normally would.
2. Open developer tools (F12) > **Application** (Chrome/Edge) or
   **Storage** (Firefox) > **Cookies** > your SharePoint domain.
3. Copy the values of the `FedAuth` and `rtFa` cookies.

```{r}
library(sharepointr)

auth <- sharepoint_auth(
  site_url = "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/MySite",
  fedauth  = Sys.getenv("SHAREPOINT_FEDAUTH"),
  rtfa     = Sys.getenv("SHAREPOINT_RTFA")
)
```

Treat these values like a password — anyone with them can act as you on
this site until they expire. Store them as environment variables (as
above) or in a secrets manager, never hardcoded in a script.

This method always uses the SharePoint REST API (`backend = "rest"` is
implied); Microsoft Graph has no concept of cookie authentication.

## Option 2/3: App registration (client secret or certificate)

For scheduled jobs, pipelines, or anything that needs to run without you
present, authenticate as an Entra ID app registration instead.

### Create the app registration

1. Go to the [Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) →
   **Identity → Applications → App registrations → New registration**.
   Give it any name — this is a headless, app-only integration, so the
   redirect URI and account type settings don't matter much.
2. Note the **Application (client) ID** and **Directory (tenant) ID** shown
   on the registration's overview page.

### Add a credential

**Client secret** — under **Certificates & secrets → Client secrets → New
client secret**. Copy the secret's **value** immediately, it's only shown
once. Secrets expire (up to 2 years) and need manual rotation.

**Certificate** — under **Certificates & secrets → Certificates → Upload
certificate**, upload the **public key** of a certificate you generate:

```bash
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -days 730 -nodes -subj "/CN=sharepointr"
cat key.pem cert.pem > combined.pem   # what certificate_path points at
```

Upload `cert.pem` to Entra ID; keep `combined.pem` (private key + cert)
somewhere safe and out of version control.

### Grant API permissions

Under **API permissions → Add a permission**, choose **Application
permissions** (not delegated — there's no signed-in user in this flow):

- **Graph backend** (recommended): `Microsoft Graph` → `Sites.Selected`
  (access granted per-site, see below) or `Sites.ReadWrite.All` (every
  site in the tenant).
- **REST backend**: `SharePoint` → `Sites.FullControl.All`, or a narrower
  permission your tenant admin has defined.

Click **Grant admin consent for {tenant}**.

If you used `Sites.Selected`, also grant the app access to your *specific*
site: tenant-wide consent alone isn't enough. Do this with the
[Graph site permissions API](https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/site-post-permissions)
or PnP PowerShell's `Grant-PnPAzureADAppSitePermission`. Skipping this step
is the most common cause of a 403 on your first real call.

### Authenticate from R

```{r}
# Client secret
auth <- sharepoint_auth(
  site_url      = "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/MySite",
  tenant_id     = "contoso.onmicrosoft.com",
  client_id     = Sys.getenv("SHAREPOINT_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("SHAREPOINT_CLIENT_SECRET")
)

# Certificate, equivalently
auth <- sharepoint_auth(
  site_url              = "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/MySite",
  tenant_id             = "contoso.onmicrosoft.com",
  client_id             = Sys.getenv("SHAREPOINT_CLIENT_ID"),
  certificate_path      = "combined.pem",
  certificate_password  = Sys.getenv("SHAREPOINT_CERT_PASSWORD") # only if the key is encrypted
)
```

Add `backend = "rest"` to either call to use the classic SharePoint REST
API instead of Graph.

## Listing, uploading, downloading, and managing files

Paths are library-relative — they include the document library name (most
often `"Shared Documents"`) but not the site URL, which `auth` already
knows. This is the same regardless of which authentication method you used.

```{r}
# List everything in a folder
sp_list_items(auth, "Shared Documents")
#>          name   type size            modified
#> 1     Reports folder   NA 2026-01-01 09:00:00
#> 2 Welcome.docx   file 8213 2025-11-03 14:22:10

sp_list_files(auth, "Shared Documents")
sp_list_folders(auth, "Shared Documents")

# Upload
sp_upload_file(auth, "report.xlsx", "Shared Documents/Reports/report.xlsx")

# Download (dest controls the local file name)
sp_download_file(auth, "Shared Documents/Reports/report.xlsx", "report.xlsx")
sp_download_file(
  auth, "Shared Documents/Reports/report.xlsx",
  dest = "downloads/renamed.xlsx"
)

# Manage
sp_create_folder(auth, "Shared Documents/Reports/2026")
sp_file_exists(auth, "Shared Documents/Reports/2026/report.xlsx")
sp_delete_item(auth, "Shared Documents/Reports/2026/report.xlsx")
```

Files larger than 4MB are uploaded via a chunked, resumable upload session
automatically when using the Graph backend — no different call needed.

Deleted items go to the site recycle bin, not permanently deleted.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Failed to parse SharePoint's response as JSON" / mentions "expired"**
  (cookie auth) — your `fedauth`/`rtfa` cookies have expired. Sign in to
  SharePoint in your browser again and copy fresh values.
- **403 Forbidden** (app registration auth) — almost always a missing
  admin consent step, or (with `Sites.Selected`) a missing per-site grant.
- **Token requests failing** (app registration auth) — double check
  `tenant_id` is the *directory* ID (a GUID) or a verified domain like
  `contoso.onmicrosoft.com`, not the SharePoint site URL.
- **"Could not find a document library named ..."** (Graph backend) — the
  first path segment must match the library as SharePoint shows it in the
  browser, e.g. `"Shared Documents"`, not the underlying Graph drive name
  (`"Documents"`).
